newsitem.title: USA: U.S. conventional mortgage rates lower in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. conventional mortgage rates lower in week.

text.p: Average commitment rates on fixed-rate mortgages fell in the week latest week to their lowest levels since December, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.

The 30-year fixed-rate loan fell to an average 7.65 percent in the week ended February 14 from 7.74 percent in the prior week. The 15-year fixed-rate loan rate fell to 7.14 percent from 7.25 percent last week, Freddie Mac said.
The 30-year loan slipped to its lowest level since 7.64 percent in the week ended December 27. The 15-year loan was at its lowest since 7.06 percent in the week ended December 13.
Rates on the adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) rose in the latest week to an average 5.52 percent from 5.51 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 6.94 percent, the 15-year 6.44 percent and the ARM 5.19 percent.

"The Federal Reserve's action to leave monetary policy unchanged should help promote an affordable mortgage market over the next few weeksd, in which case we expect to see a rebound in the (home sales) figures," Freddie Mac Deputy Chief Economist Frank Nothaft said.
The Federal Reserve last week decided not to increase interest rates that would mean higher mortgage rates for new home buyers.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.3 percent ARM loans this week, down from 1.4 percent last week.
